title: 一天被问七百遍，机器人怎么听清你？
title_en: 700 questions a day: how does a robot hear you?

segments.zh: 七百个问题。一台机器人，在医院导诊台，一天要回答七百个问题。
segments.en: Seven hundred questions. A robot at a hospital help desk answers 700 questions a day.

segments.zh: 我猜，其中三百个是：厕所在哪？
segments.en: My guess: three hundred of them are 'where's the bathroom?'

segments.zh: 据报道，这是一台半人高的人形机器人，
segments.en: Reportedly, it's a half-size humanoid robot,

segments.zh: 最近站上了一家三甲医院的导诊台。
segments.en: now staffing the help desk of a top-tier hospital.

segments.zh: 今天的主角：小导。它管指路、管流程、管医保。
segments.en: Today's star: Little Guide. Directions, procedures, insurance questions.

segments.zh: 算一下：一天八小时，七百个问题，
segments.en: Do the math: 700 questions in an eight-hour day

segments.zh: 大约每四十秒，就有一个人冲它开口。
segments.en: is one every forty seconds or so.

segments.zh: 今天的烧脑问题：医院大厅那么吵，它怎么听清你说的话？
segments.en: Today's brain teaser: in a noisy hospital lobby, how does it hear you?

segments.zh: 先看有多吵。大厅里叫号、脚步、聊天，估计有六七十分贝。
segments.en: First, how noisy? Number calls, footsteps, chatter: maybe 60 to 70 decibels.

segments.zh: 而你对它说话，也就六十分贝左右。噪声，和你一样大。
segments.en: And you talking to it? About 60 decibels. The noise is as loud as you are.

segments.zh: 分贝每加十，声音的能量就乘十。七十比六十，能量是十倍。
segments.en: Every 10 decibels means ten times the energy. 70 versus 60 is ten times as much.

segments.zh: 人是怎么做到的？鸡尾酒会效应：
segments.en: How do people manage? The cocktail party effect:

segments.zh: 一屋子人在说话，你还是能听清对面那一个。
segments.en: a room full of talk, and you still follow one voice.

segments.zh: 秘诀之一：两只耳朵。声音从左边来，左耳先听到，右耳晚一点。
segments.en: Secret one: two ears. Sound from the left hits the left ear first, the right ear a bit later.

segments.zh: 大脑靠这一点点时间差，就知道声音从哪儿来。
segments.en: From that tiny delay, your brain knows where the sound came from.

segments.zh: 小导没有耳朵，它头上有一圈麦克风，叫麦克风阵列。
segments.en: Little Guide has no ears. It has a ring of microphones: a microphone array.

segments.zh: 声速每秒三百四十米。
segments.en: Sound travels 340 meters per second.

segments.zh: 两个麦克风隔五厘米，时间差最多零点一五毫秒。
segments.en: Mics 5 cm apart hear it at most 0.15 milliseconds apart.

segments.zh: 这么小的差，电脑也量得出来。于是，它知道你站在哪个方向。
segments.en: Tiny, but a computer can measure it. So it knows which direction you're standing in.

segments.zh: 反转一：知道方向，还不够。噪声照样往里灌。
segments.en: Twist one: knowing the direction isn't enough. The noise still pours in.

segments.zh: 下一招叫波束成形。打个比方：一群人齐步走。
segments.en: The next trick is beamforming. Think of a crowd marching in step.

segments.zh: 把每个麦克风的声音，按你的时间差对齐，再加起来。
segments.en: Line up every mic's sound by your time delay, then add them together.

segments.zh: 你的声音，步子对齐了，越加越响。
segments.en: Your voice is in step, so it adds up and gets louder.

segments.zh: 四面八方的噪声，步子对不齐，加起来有的抵消，涨得慢。
segments.en: Noise from everywhere else is out of step. Some cancels out, and it grows more slowly.

segments.zh: 理想情况下，六个麦克风，你的声音比噪声，能提高六倍，
segments.en: Ideally, six mics boost your voice over the noise six times,

segments.zh: 大约八分贝。这是估算。
segments.en: about 8 decibels. That's an estimate.

segments.zh: 相当于，在嘈杂的大厅里，给你一个人开了一束看不见的手电筒。
segments.en: It's like an invisible flashlight, shining only on you in the noisy hall.

segments.zh: 反转二：听清了，还得听懂。
segments.en: Twist two: hearing you isn't the same as understanding you.

segments.zh: 第一步，把声音变成文字：“请问心内科在几楼？”
segments.en: Step one: turn sound into text. 'Which floor is cardiology?'

segments.zh: 第二步，AI 理解你在问什么：找科室。
segments.en: Step two: the AI works out what you want: a department.

segments.zh: 第三步最关键：它不凭记忆回答，
segments.en: Step three is the key: it doesn't answer from memory.

segments.zh: 而是先去翻医院的资料。
segments.en: It looks it up first.

segments.zh: 这就像开卷考试：书里写着心内科在三楼，它才说三楼。
segments.en: Like an open-book exam: the book says third floor, so it says third floor.

segments.zh: 为什么要开卷？
segments.en: Why open-book?

segments.zh: 因为大模型闭卷考试，偶尔会一本正经地瞎编。
segments.en: Because a big AI model, taking the test closed-book, sometimes makes things up with a straight face.

segments.zh: 在医院里，编错一个楼层，病人就要多爬三层楼。
segments.en: In a hospital, one wrong floor means a patient climbs three extra flights.

segments.zh: 反转三，最反直觉：好的导诊机器人，要知道什么不该答。
segments.en: Twist three, the counterintuitive one: a good guide robot knows what not to answer.

segments.zh: 报道里，它管的是指路、流程、医保。看病，还是交给医生。
segments.en: In the reports, it handles directions, procedures, insurance. Diagnosis stays with the doctors.

segments.zh: 那为什么要做成人形，而不是一块大屏幕？
segments.en: So why make it humanoid, instead of just a big screen?

segments.zh: 我的推测：人更愿意跟像人的东西说话，
segments.en: My guess: people talk more easily to something human-shaped,

segments.zh: 而且它能转身，能抬手给你指方向。
segments.en: and it can turn and point the way.

segments.zh: 半人高也有讲究：老人、坐轮椅的人、小朋友，都能平视它。这也是推测。
segments.en: Half height may matter too: seniors, wheelchair users, kids can look it in the eye. Also a guess.

segments.zh: 再回到七百个问题。
segments.en: Back to the 700 questions.

segments.zh: 人回答七百遍，嗓子哑了，脾气也没了。
segments.en: A person answering 700 times loses their voice, and their patience.

segments.zh: 小导回答第七百遍，和第一遍一样耐心。
segments.en: Little Guide answers the 700th time as patiently as the first.

segments.zh: 这可能才是它最大的本事：不累，不烦。
segments.en: That may be its real superpower: it never gets tired or grumpy.

segments.zh: 算总账：听方向，靠时间差。
segments.en: Final tally: direction comes from the time delay.

segments.zh: 听清楚，靠波束成形。
segments.en: Hearing clearly comes from beamforming.

segments.zh: 答对，靠开卷考试。
segments.en: Getting it right comes from the open book.

segments.zh: 不乱答，靠知道自己的边界。
segments.en: Not getting it wrong comes from knowing its limits.

segments.zh: 友情提示：七百问是报道的数字，
segments.en: Friendly fine print: 700 is the reported number.

segments.zh: 分贝和信噪比是我们的估算。
segments.en: The decibels and the gain are our estimates.

segments.zh: 这台机器人内部用什么算法，没有公开。我们讲的是通用的原理。
segments.en: Its exact algorithms aren't public. We explained the general principles.

segments.zh: 最后，小导想说：厕所在您左手边，直走二十米。
segments.en: Finally, Little Guide would like to say: the bathroom is on your left, twenty meters ahead.

segments.zh: 这是今天的第七百零一遍。
segments.en: That's the seven hundred and first time today.
